# dtrsv

> Solves one of the systems of equations A·x = b, or Aᵀ·x = b.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dtrsv from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/dtrsv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dtrsv( order, uplo, trans, diag, N, A, LDA, x, strideX ) → Float64Array
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | `'no-transpose'` or `'transpose'` |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | in |  | one of `'non-unit'`, `'unit'` | `'unit'` or `'non-unit'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | `x` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: On entry, `UPLO` specifies whether the matrix is an upper or lower triangular matrix as follows:

  `UPLO = 'U'` or 'u' A is an upper triangular matrix.

  `UPLO = 'L'` or 'l' A is a lower triangular matrix.
- `trans`: On entry, `TRANS` specifies the equations to be solved as follows:

  $$
  \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'N'} \quad\text{or}\quad \text{'n'} A \, x = b
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'T'} \quad\text{or}\quad \text{'t'} A^T \, x = b
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'C'} \quad\text{or}\quad \text{'c'} A^T \, x = b
  $$
- `diag`: On entry, `DIAG` specifies whether or not A is unit triangular as follows:

  `DIAG = 'U'` or 'u' A is assumed to be unit triangular.

  `DIAG = 'N'` or 'n' A is not assumed to be unit

  triangular.
- `N`: On entry, N specifies the order of the matrix A. N must be at least zero.
- `A`: Before entry with `UPLO = 'U'` or 'u', the leading n by n upper triangular part of the array A must contain the upper triangular matrix and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. Before entry with `UPLO = 'L'` or 'l', the leading n by n lower triangular part of the array A must contain the lower triangular matrix and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. Note that when `DIAG = 'U'` or 'u', the diagonal elements of A are not referenced either, but are assumed to be unity.
- `x`: ( 1 + ( n - 1 )\*abs( `INCX` ) ). Before entry, the incremented array X must contain the n element right-hand side vector b. On exit, X is overwritten with the solution vector x.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: output array

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be non-zero

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dtrsv.ndarray(
    uplo, trans, diag,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    x, strideX, offsetX
) → Float64Array
```

Solves one of the systems of equations `A*x = b` or `A**T*x = b` where `A` is an `N` by `N` upper or lower triangular matrix.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | specifies whether `A` is upper or lower triangular |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | specifies the operation to be performed |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | in |  | one of `'non-unit'`, `'unit'` | specifies whether `A` is unit or non-unit triangular |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix `A` |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `A` |
| `x` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N` |  | input/output vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | `x` stride length |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `x` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: On entry, `UPLO` specifies whether the matrix is an upper or lower triangular matrix as follows:

  `UPLO = 'U'` or 'u' A is an upper triangular matrix.

  `UPLO = 'L'` or 'l' A is a lower triangular matrix.
- `trans`: On entry, `TRANS` specifies the equations to be solved as follows:

  $$
  \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'N'} \quad\text{or}\quad \text{'n'} A \, x = b
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'T'} \quad\text{or}\quad \text{'t'} A^T \, x = b
  $$

  $$
  \mathrm{TRANS} = \text{'C'} \quad\text{or}\quad \text{'c'} A^T \, x = b
  $$
- `diag`: On entry, `DIAG` specifies whether or not A is unit triangular as follows:

  `DIAG = 'U'` or 'u' A is assumed to be unit triangular.

  `DIAG = 'N'` or 'n' A is not assumed to be unit

  triangular.
- `N`: On entry, N specifies the order of the matrix A. N must be at least zero.
- `A`: Before entry with `UPLO = 'U'` or 'u', the leading n by n upper triangular part of the array A must contain the upper triangular matrix and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. Before entry with `UPLO = 'L'` or 'l', the leading n by n lower triangular part of the array A must contain the lower triangular matrix and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. Note that when `DIAG = 'U'` or 'u', the diagonal elements of A are not referenced either, but are assumed to be unity.
- `x`: ( 1 + ( n - 1 )\*abs( `INCX` ) ). Before entry, the incremented array X must contain the n element right-hand side vector b. On exit, X is overwritten with the solution vector x.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `x`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be non-zero

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dtrsv from './../lib/base.js';

// Solve A*x = b for triangular A:
const A = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 3.0, 0.0, 4.0 ] );
const x = new Float64Array( [ 5.0, 4.0 ] );

dtrsv( 'upper', 'no-transpose', 'non-unit', 2, A, 2, 1, 0, x, 1, 0 );
console.log( x ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `DTRSV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DTRSV solves one of the systems of equations

$$
A \, x = b, \quad\text{or}\quad A^T \, x = b
$$

where b and x are n element vectors and A is an n by n unit, or non-unit, upper or lower triangular matrix.

No test for singularity or near-singularity is included in this routine. Such tests must be performed before calling this routine.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
